package_info.why_malicious: The package was intentionally crafted to exploit a path traversal vulnerability in the CDNJS update automation, enabling arbitrary file write and remote code execution on the CDNJS infrastructure. This could lead to full compromise of the CDN, affecting millions of websites.

execution_context.trigger: autoupdate/CI-CD (CDNJS bot processing new npm package versions)
execution_context.file_location: npm package tarball (hey-sven-1.0.1.tgz) with malicious file paths

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During automated package extraction, the archive writes a shell script to an arbitrary location outside the intended directory using path traversal, enabling arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of path traversal in archive file paths is a classic exploitation technique to escape the intended extraction directory and overwrite or create files elsewhere on the system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should only contain files within their own directory structure. Writing files to arbitrary locations is never expected.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Path traversal in archives is never legitimate in package distribution.
key_indicators: Files written outside the package directory
Presence of executable scripts in unexpected locations

execution_context.trigger: autoupdate/CI-CD (CDNJS bot processing new npm package versions)
execution_context.file_location: npm package tarball (hey-sven-1.0.1.tgz) with malicious symlink

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: symlink in git repo pointing to sensitive file (e.g., /etc/passwd or config file)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During package extraction, a symlink is created that points to a sensitive file, allowing subsequent read operations to access arbitrary files on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Symlinks in package archives can be abused to access or overwrite files outside the intended directory, leading to information disclosure or privilege escalation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not contain symlinks to sensitive system files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Symlinks are sometimes used within package directories, but never to point outside the package scope.
key_indicators: Symlinks pointing to sensitive or system files

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when malicious script is executed by the server)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script reads sensitive environment variables or secret files and writes their contents to a publicly accessible location, enabling secret exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating secrets is a clear sign of malicious intent, especially when secrets are written to public directories.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal scripts should not access or leak secrets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use for leaking secrets to public files.
key_indicators: Access to secret files or environment variables
Writing secrets to public or external locations

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious npm package (hey-sven) with crafted archive paths and/or symlinks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious files and symlinks are extracted on the CDNJS update server.

attack_chain.action: CDNJS autoupdate bot processes the new package version, extracting the archive and writing files outside the intended directory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious shell script and/or symlink is placed on the server.

attack_chain.action: Malicious shell script is executed by the server, reading sensitive secrets and exfiltrating them to a public location.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive API keys and tokens.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses stolen credentials (GITHUB_REPO_API_KEY, WORKERS_KV_API_TOKEN) to tamper with CDNJS libraries, cache, or website.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of CDNJS infrastructure and potential supply-chain attack on all dependent websites.

behavioral_signatures: Archive extraction with path traversal (../../../) in file paths
Symlinks in package archives pointing outside the package directory
Unexpected file writes to /tmp or other system directories during package processing
Execution of scripts extracted from package archives
file_indicators: npm package tarballs with ../../../ in file paths
Presence of symlinks in package archives
Unexpected shell scripts in /tmp or other non-package directories
network_indicators: Unusual access to public URLs serving sensitive data (e.g., /cdnjs/public/ryotak.txt)
Outbound connections or uploads from the update server after package extraction
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for package archives containing path traversal sequences or symlinks during extraction. Alert on any file writes outside the intended package directory, especially to system or temporary directories. Detect execution of scripts that originate from package archives. Monitor for access or exfiltration of sensitive secrets to public or external locations. Implement strict validation and sandboxing of automated package processing bots.
